title: Findings: the CI gate's verdict on a pull request, and the checks behind it
description: Written by the gate's verify step (expectrail.gate.verify), in the job that runs the pull request's code. Read by the gate's comment step (expectrail.gate.comment), in a separate job that treats it as untrusted data: it is size-capped, parsed with duplicate keys and non-finite numbers refused, checked against this schema with the standard-library validator in expectrail.gate.record, and checked for consistency (every finding id is recomputed, every count recounted, the decision decided again). Held-out routes appear as counts only: this schema has no place for their names.

decision.description: accept only when at least one check ran and every public and held-out check passes, and, for a change declared a fix (intent), a check also demonstrated the repair; any failure rejects; anything else needs review

adapter.description: how the game was replayed: the name of the engine adapter in the registry (harness/adapters.py), as the verify request names it. The gate writes a record only for an adapter that has a verify path; godot is the one that has today

path.description: the Godot project folder, relative to the repository root (. for the root)

checksFrom.description: base: the specs and routes were read from the pull request's base commit, so the change cannot edit the checks that judge it

checksChanged.description: spec and route files that differ between the base and the head (added, removed or edited), counted, not named

drafts.description: spec files without a person's approval, which never judge a change

checkProblems.description: problems the gate found reading the spec and route files (a file refused or not valid, an id or a name used twice, a limit passed, nothing found where it was told to look), each named in the reasons. Above 0 the decision is never accept: the checks that ran are not all of the project's checks. Absent from records written before November 12, 2026, where such a problem did not change the decision; a reader takes an absent count as 0.

observers.description: which observers judged the checks. both: the engine's record and a visual observer over the captured frames judge every check, and no check passes on the engine's record alone (issue #327). engine-only: the engine's record alone. Written under both only: an engine-only record has no block, as before the block existed (November 12, 2026), so an older reader still reads it, and a reader takes an absent block as engine-only.

visual.description: the visual observer that was asked; null when none was (under both, nothing is then accepted)

intent.description: What the change was declared as (issue #284). fix: it claims to fix a reported bug, and is accepted only when the repair block shows a demonstration. change: an intended change of behaviour. none: nothing declared. change and none are judged alike, by the rule that held before this field. Written only when it is fix or change: a record with no intent declared nothing, as every record before November 12, 2026 did, and a reader takes an absent intent as none.

repair.description: Given exactly when intent is fix. One row for every check that failed on the base and passes after the change, with every run on each side. A row counts when the base failed on all of its runs and the head passed on all of its runs. A fix is accepted only when at least one row counts; with none the decision is needs-review with the reason repair-not-demonstrated (or reject, when a check fails after the change).

runs.description: runs a side that a demonstration needs

base.description: the check's result on the base on each run; the first is the row's before

head.description: the check's result after the change on each run; the first is the row's after

counts.description: true when the base failed and the head passed on every one of the runs
the public checks after the change; needsReview includes replay errors

checks.description: one row per approved spec on each public route

before.description: on the base commit; null when the base was not replayed

comparison.description: the review's words (docs/review.md); anything but pass or fail on either side is INCONCLUSIVE

findingId.description: null when the check passes after the change

observed.description: what each of the two observers said about this check, on each side. On every row when observers.rule is both, and then before and after follow from it (expectrail.gate.record.combine): a pass needs both to pass, a failure on either is a failure, anything else needs review. Absent under engine-only.

before.description: null when the base was not replayed

engine.description: the evaluator's result on the engine's record (the position log)

visual.description: the evaluator's result on the visual observer's observations of the captured frames; no-answer when the observer gave none (no frames, the model failed); not-asked when no visual observer was configured, the replay did not finish, or the engine's record had already failed the check

visualAnswerSha256.description: the digest of the observations document the visual observer gave (in the artifact under observations/), so its verdict can be read again without asking the model; null unless it gave a verdict

engine.description: the evaluator's result on the engine's record (the position log)

visual.description: the evaluator's result on the visual observer's observations of the captured frames; no-answer when the observer gave none (no frames, the model failed); not-asked when no visual observer was configured, the replay did not finish, or the engine's record had already failed the check

visualAnswerSha256.description: the digest of the observations document the visual observer gave (in the artifact under observations/), so its verdict can be read again without asking the model; null unless it gave a verdict

findings.description: one per check that does not pass after the change

id.description: the first 12 hex digits of sha256(spec + LF + route + LF + kind): the same failure keeps its id across pushes

frame.description: the first failing frame after the change, when the evaluator names one

heldOut.description: counts only: no route names, files, frames or reasons

isolation.description: Whether the game ran in the replay sandbox (docs/replay-sandbox.md), over every replay this record rests on: head, base and held-out. Counts and the tool only. Absent from records written before November 12, 2026, which a reader treats as not isolated.

replays.description: Replays that finished and were judged.

sandboxed.description: How many of them ran inside the sandbox: no network, own process tree, only the game's own files.

required.description: True when the gate was told to refuse to replay outside the sandbox.

sandbox.description: The tool that isolated the sandboxed replays; null when none was.

reasons.description: Why replays ran outside the sandbox, each distinct reason once.

generatedChecks.description: Optional and advisory (docs/jit.md): checks generated for this change. The decision rule never reads it; the decision follows from counts and heldOut alone.

reviewPage.description: the review page's path inside the artifact

commit.description: the Expectrail commit the action was pinned to, when it was used by commit
